Answer: B) Bochdalek hernia with herniated abdominal contents  
Reason: In Figure 1 (PA view), a well-circumscribed rounded opacity is seen at the left costophrenic angle, abutting the diaphragm; in Figure 5 (lateral view), this opacity lies posterior to the heart and anterior to the spine, with visible bowel gas patterns within it—consistent with intra-thoracic abdominal contents herniating through a posterolateral diaphragmatic defect (Bochdalek hernia), rather than a pleural effusion (which would layer dependently), lipoma (no fat density), nodule (no internal gas), hiatal hernia (typically midline/retrocardiac), or pseudotumor (no associated volume loss or fissure shift).
